arms.diagnostic_note: The multi-city Or-opt (segments 1-3) with grid-guided insertion, rebalanced move mix (55/10/35), and cooler SA temperature (N*3 vs N*2) did not produce a measurable improvement over single-city Or-opt. Possible causes: (1) Grid-guided insertion still picks targets that are too far in tour-position, causing many moves to be skipped (rlen>500 check). (2) The overhead of computing centroid and grid lookup for multi-city segments offsets the benefit. (3) Single-city Or-opt already captures most available relocation improvements at this tour quality level. (4) The cooler SA temperature reduces acceptance of uphill moves that would enable the multi-city moves to eventually improve. The 71.40 outlier in run3 is consistent with known ±5-point machine load variance on the 2s time limit.

discrepancy_analysis: h-main's multi-city Or-opt with grid-guided insertion did not measurably outperform single-city Or-opt. The effect size, if any, is smaller than the ~0.4-point run-to-run variance. The mechanism (compound relocations + spatial targeting) did not translate into score gains, likely because: (a) at this tour quality level, single-city relocations already find most productive moves, and (b) the grid-guided targeting doesn't consistently pick better targets than the random shift. The 71.40 outlier in h-main run3 is attributed to machine load (the control never dropped below 78.49).
